title: I loose the noose that Nirṛti bound

words.meaning: Nirṛti, the goddess of decay and dissolution

words.gram: present, 1st sg. active (s becomes ṣ after vi)
words.role: main verb of the second line

words.meaning: like, as it were (Vedic comparative na)
words.role: compares the release to one from the middle of life
words.context: Sāyaṇa reads it as a negation: not from the middle of life only, but for the whole of it

words.role: main verb of the last clause

sandhi.rule: i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y; -aḥ before n becomes -o
t before a vowel becomes d
a final m joins the following vowel

morphology.note: the s of syāmi (√so, ‘to bind’, with vi ‘to unbind’) becomes ṣ after the preverb vi; the word is given in its recited form.
Vedic lengthening of the final vowel of atha (P. 6.3.136 (निपातस्य च)).

translation.literal: The cord, not to be loosed, which the goddess Nirṛti bound on your neck — this of yours I untie, as from the middle of life; then, living, eat food, set free.
translation.readable: The noose that cannot be loosed, that the goddess Nirṛti tied about your neck — I untie it for you. Now, freed and alive, eat your food.

meaning: A releasing verse: the speaker unties the noose that Nirṛti, the goddess of decay, tied on a person’s neck, and bids him, freed and alive, eat his food. Sāyaṇa reads it as addressed to the sacrificer, whose bonds of evil are loosed. In the Navagraha sūktam it is the third mantra for Rāhu, before the salutation; the witness names the graha’s adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together and does not say which mantra is whose.
in_the_rite: Step 8 (Rāhu), third mantra. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Saṃhitā (TS 4.2.5.3) it belongs to the piling of the fire altar: three black bricks for Nirṛti are covered with a net and laid away from the altar (Sāyaṇa’s viniyoga).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa cites the Kalpa: «यत्ते देवी निर्ऋतिराबबन्धेति शिक्वजालेनैनाः प्रच्छाद्य», the bricks are covered with a net with this verse.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa addresses the verse to the sacrificer: Nirṛti has bound on his neck «निर्ऋतिर्देवी यद्दाम स्वकीयं पाशमविचर्त्यं विनाशयितुमशक्यम्»; the speaker says «तदिदं ते दाम त्वदीयग्रीवास्थं पाशं विष्यामि विमुञ्चामि», and then «त्वं जीवीश्चिरंजीवी सन्प्रमुक्तः सर्वैः प्रतिबन्धैर्विरहितः पितुमन्नमद्धि भक्षय». The bricks themselves are Nirṛti’s, black and baked with husks: «नैर्ऋतिः कृष्णास्रिस्रस्तुषपक्वा भवन्ति».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh. The base writes the preverb apart (निर्ऋतिरा बबन्ध), as Sāyaṇa’s Kalpa quotation joins it (आबबन्ध).
